Three changes to sdkconfig.defaults:

description:
## Why
The current 1:1 button→switch mapping wastes Up/Down as dedicated switch endpoints. The new model uses Up/Down for navigation and Mid as the action button, enabling 3 virtual switches from one physical action button. The e-ink display should be useful post-commissioning rather than showing a static QR forever.

## What needs to be done

### app_priv.h
- Add `void app_display_show_switch(int switch_num);` declaration
- Change `app_driver_buttons_init` signature to accept display callback: `esp_err_t app_driver_buttons_init(uint16_t *endpoint_ids, void (*on_switch_selected)(int));`
- SWITCH_x_IDX constants stay (GPIO order), semantic meaning changes

### app_main.cpp
- Change switch labels: {"Up", "Down", "Mid"} → {"1", "2", "3"}
- Add `app_display_show_switch(int n)` — draws "Switch N" big/centered on e-ink
- After `esp_matter::start()`, check FabricCount():
  - == 0 → show QR code (existing path)
  - > 0 → call `app_display_show_switch(1)` (already commissioned at boot)
- In `kCommissioningComplete` event → call `app_display_show_switch(1)`
- Pass `app_display_show_switch` as callback to `app_driver_buttons_init`

### app_driver.cpp
- Add `static int s_selected_switch = 0;` (0-indexed)
- Add `static void (*s_display_cb)(int) = nullptr;`
- Up button: `s_selected_switch = (s_selected_switch + 1) % 3` → call display cb. No Matter events.
- Down button: `s_selected_switch = (s_selected_switch + 2) % 3` → call display cb. No Matter events.
- Mid button: fire InitialPress/ShortRelease on `s_endpoint_ids[s_selected_switch]` (dynamic)
- Long-press factory reset stays on Mid only
- LED flash on Up/Down for tactile feedback (keep existing brief-flash)

## What stays the same
- 3 Generic Switch endpoints with Fixed Label cluster
- InitialPress + ShortRelease event sequence (Apple Home compatible)
- Long-press Mid → factory reset
- LED blink states (fast=uncommissioned, slow=commissioned)
- NVS, QR rendering infrastructure

## Files touched
- main/app_priv.h
- main/app_main.cpp
- main/app_driver.cpp
title: Redesign: selector+action button model with post-commission display

design:
- SPI3 (VSPI) host, 1 MHz, mode 0
- GPIO map: MOSI=23, SCK=18, CS=9, DC=15, RST=0, BUSY=4
- BUSY pin INVERTED: LOW=busy, HIGH=ready
- Two DMA-capable heap buffers (2×5000 bytes): s_buf (new) + s_old_buf (previous frame)
- Hardware reset: RST low 10ms → high 10ms
- Full JD79653A init sequence: Panel Setting, FitiPower internals, resolution, TCON, VCOM, power-on, 5 LUT tables
- Full refresh only (DTM1=old, DTM2=new, cmd 0x12, ~820ms)

description:
## Why
The 16-switch NVS config (line1, line2, enabled) has no user-facing way to be changed. Need a browser-based tool using Web Serial API + CBOR protocol to read/write switch config via USB-serial.

## Architecture
Browser (Web Serial API) <-> UART0 @ 115200 <-> ESP32 command handler (app_serial.cpp)
Web app: web/index.html (self-contained HTML+JS, CBOR+SLIP framing)

## Serial Protocol
Framing: SLIP (RFC 1055) - 0xC0 delimiters around CBOR payloads, distinguishes from ASCII log lines.

Commands (web -> device):
- {"cmd": "read"} - read all 16 slot configs
- {"cmd": "write", "slots": {"0": {"l1": "Kitchen", "l2": "Light", "en": true}, ...}} - write specific slots
- {"cmd": "reboot"} - esp_restart()

Responses (device -> web):
- {"status": "ok", "slots": [{"l1": "Switch", "l2": "1", "en": true}, ...]} - 16 entries
- {"status": "error", "msg": "l1 too long"}

## Validation
Firmware write: l1/l2 max 8 chars non-empty, en=bool, at least 1 slot enabled
Firmware boot: truncate long strings, clamp sel_sw, force slot 0 if none enabled

## New Files
- main/app_serial.cpp - UART command handler task (SLIP+CBOR+NVS)
- main/app_serial.h - esp_err_t app_serial_init(void)
- web/index.html - self-contained Web Serial configurator

## Modified Files
- main/app_main.cpp - call app_serial_init()
- main/app_driver.cpp - boot-time NVS validation
- main/CMakeLists.txt - add app_serial.cpp

## Verification
1. Build, flash. Device boots with normal log output.
2. Open web/index.html in Chrome, click Connect, pick serial port.
3. Read from Device -> table populates with NVS config.
4. Modify slots, Write to Device -> device reboots with new config.
5. Edge cases: empty strings, 8+ chars, disable all (rejected).
title: Web Serial + CBOR switch configurator

acceptance_criteria: LED blinks fast before commissioning, transitions to slow blink after kCommissioningComplete fires
description: Replace direct LED on/off calls with a background blink driver so the LED communicates commissioning state at a glance.
design:
Implementation: esp_timer periodic timer toggling GPIO10.

New API (in app_driver.cpp / app_priv.h):
  void app_driver_led_blink_start(uint32_t half_period_ms)  // starts/restarts timer
  void app_driver_led_blink_stop(void)                       // stops timer + LED off

Blink rates:
  FAST = 250 ms half-period (2 Hz) — no fabric / commissioning window open
  SLOW = 1000 ms half-period (0.5 Hz) — commissioned

Event mapping in app_event_cb:
  kCommissioningWindowOpened  → fast blink (250 ms)
  kCommissioningWindowClosed  → stop blink
  kCommissioningComplete      → slow blink (1000 ms)
  kFabricRemoved (count==0)   → fast blink (250 ms)  [window re-opens automatically]

Boot: start fast blink if WiFi not yet provisioned (after esp_matter::start()).

Identification callback: fast blink on START/EFFECT; stop on STOP.

Remove direct app_driver_led_set() calls from app_event_cb and app_identification_cb; keep app_driver_led_set() as internal primitive.
title: LED blink: fast=uncommissioned, slow=commissioned
